issues.failure_explanation: On I^j, phi = jh+delta^mu+(h-delta^mu)P(...). Monotonicity needs the coefficient h-delta^mu > 0, not just P'>0. Lemma 2.1 imposes no condition, and phi decreases on I^j if delta^mu > h. Theorem 2.2 allows h = delta^mu, where psi_q is constant on every I_q^j. Then psi_q is not strictly increasing, and psi_q' vanishes on whole intervals, not only at endpoints. The numerical tests use exactly this degenerate case h = delta^mu.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume h > delta^mu in Lemma 2.1 and Theorem 2.2, and note that the experiments correspond to the excluded degenerate case.
issues.overall_effect: The strict-monotonicity claims and the claim that derivatives vanish only at endpoints fail for h <= delta^mu. The experiments test piecewise-constant inner functions, the very feature criticized in Igelnik-Parikh.
issues.title: Strict monotonicity of phi and psi_q fails unless h > delta^mu
issues.why_classification: Adding a strict inequality is a local condition; the construction and the stated bounds survive for h > delta^mu.

issues.failure_explanation: a_q^j = 0 for j=(-1,...,-1) and a_q^j = |lambda|_1 for j=(J-1,...,J-1), at every q. More generally, any j with entries in {-1,J-1} gives a q-independent value, so images at different levels coincide. Within a level, psi_q(c) = j h + (h+delta^mu)/2 - phi((1-q)delta) involves delta^mu, which need not be rational. Rational independence of lambda then does not exclude equalities such as lambda_1/lambda_2 = (h+K_q)/K_q. The cited Lorentz lemma is a genericity statement and cannot be applied to a specific y.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to a fixed q. Require h and delta^mu rational so that all psi_q(c_q^{j_p}) are rational, and prove distinctness by rational independence plus strict monotonicity.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that all a_q^j are distinct (and Remark dist-again) is false across levels and unsupported within a level for general mu.
issues.title: Distinctness of all center images is false across levels and unproved within a level
issues.why_classification: Part of the stated result must be withdrawn and the rest needs an extra hypothesis and a new argument; it is not used critically downstream.

issues.failure_explanation: Rule (chooseboxA) equates a center image with a minimum of distances, so it is malformed, and uniqueness of sigma* is unjustified when ties occur. The selected pair [tau_k, tau_{k+1}] need not contain Psi_q(x), so S is evaluated outside [0,1]. Remark 2.6's claim that Psi_q(x) avoids the tail-head gaps is false. With Sprecher-like lambda, x_2 in a gap (or near the end of I^{j_2} when h > delta^mu) makes Psi_q(x) sweep across the gap between rows. As Psi_q(x) crosses midpoints between images from different rows, the selected row switches. g_q then jumps between values like f(1,c^{j_2})/N and f(0,c^{j_2+1})/N, which are the paper's own jumps. So g_q is not continuous, let alone C^2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must give a well-defined univariate g_q on [0,|lambda|_1] that is C^2 across row transitions and consistent with the interpolation data, and prove its smoothness.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm does not define a univariate C^2 outer function. The headline claims of C^2 outer functions and C^2 superpositions g_q∘Psi_q (abstract, feature (ii)) are unsupported.
issues.title: Outer-function evaluation rule is ill-defined and does not yield C^2 outer functions
issues.why_classification: A central advertised property (C^2 outer functions/superpositions) fails, and restoring it requires a new outer-function construction.

issues.failure_explanation: The center is selected by nearest image in 1D, not in space, yet (Oscf3) asserts ||x-c|| <= sqrt(d)Nδ/2. Kolmogorov maps scramble locality: the nearest image can belong to a cube at spatial distance O(1), for example the next row's head (0,c^{j_2+1}) when x=(~1,·). The q in Q estimate also assumes the selected cube is the one containing x and that Psi_q(x) lies in [tau_k,tau_{k+1}]. For h > delta^mu, Psi_q(C_q^j) has length |lambda|_1(h-delta^mu), far exceeding row spacings such as lambda_1 h, so other cubes can be selected. For levels where x lies in a gap, only |f/N - g_q∘Psi_q| <= 2||f||_∞/N is available.

Also |c_q^0 - c_q^{-1}| = (h+δ)/2+(q-1)δ and |1-c_q^{J-2}| can approach 3h/2, exceeding the bound Nδ used in (bqjest).
